name: Should I replace plumbing when remodeling a kitchen?

mainEntity.name: Should I replace old plumbing lines when remodeling a kitchen in an older Los Angeles home?
mainEntity.text: Should I replace old plumbing lines when remodeling a kitchen in an older Los Angeles home?

acceptedAnswer.text: If plumbing lines are old, corroded, leaking, or difficult to access, replacing them during a kitchen remodel is often a smart decision. Once walls and floors are open, it is much easier to upgrade supply lines, drains, shutoff valves, and connections than to return later and disturb finished surfaces. This is especially relevant in older Los Angeles homes where original plumbing may be reaching the end of its useful life. Homeowners should ask the contractor and plumber to inspect the condition of existing lines before finalizing the scope. If the kitchen layout is changing, plumbing replacement may also be the most efficient time to correct poor drain slopes, reroute sink placement, or improve water pressure. The downside is added cost upfront, but the benefit is lower risk of leaks, fewer emergency repairs, and better long-term reliability. The decision should be based on age, condition, access, and the scope of the remodel.
acceptedAnswer.description: If plumbing lines are old, corroded, or hard to access, replacing them during a kitchen remodel can prevent future leaks and reduce the cost of opening finished walls later. It is especially worth considering when walls are already exposed.
